blocks.text: [1] [Arabic, p. 192] [^n3533]And when Pilate heard this saying, he took Jesus out, and sat on the tribune in the place which was called the pavement of stones, but in the Hebrew [2] called Gabbatha. [^n3534]And that day was the Friday of the passover: and it had reached [3] about the sixth hour.[^n3535] [^n3536]And he said to the Jews, Behold, your King! And they cried out, Take him, take him, crucify him, crucify him. Pilate said unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests said unto him, We have no king except [4] Cæsar. [^n3537]And Pilate, when he saw it, and[^n3538] he was gaining nothing, but the tumult was increasing, took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, and said, I [5] am innocent of the blood of this innocent man: ye shall know.[^n3539] [^n3540]And all the people [6] answered and said, His blood be on us, and on our children. [^n3541]Then Pilate commanded to grant them their request; and delivered up Jesus to be crucified, according to their wish.

[7] [^n3542]Then Judas the betrayer, when he saw Jesus wronged, went and returned the [8] thirty pieces of money to the chief priests and the elders, [^n3543]and said, I have sinned in my betraying innocent blood. And they said unto him, And we, what must we do? [9] know thou. [^n3544]And he threw down the money in the temple, and departed; and he [10] went away[^n3545] and hanged[^n3546] himself. [^n3547]And the chief priests took the money, and said, We have not authority to cast it into the place of the offering,[^n3548] for it is the price [11] of blood. [^n3549]And they took counsel, and bought with it the plain of the potter, for [12] the burial of strangers. [^n3550]Therefore that plain was called, The field of blood, unto [13] [Arabic, p. 193] this day. [^n3551]Therein[^n3552] was fulfilled the saying in the prophet which said, I took thirty pieces of money, the price of the precious one, which was fixed [14] by the children of Israel; [^n3553]and I paid them for the plain of the potter, as the Lord commanded me.

[15] [^n3554]And the Jews took Jesus, and went away to crucify him. [^n3555]And when he bare his [16] cross and went out, they stripped him of those purple and scarlet garments which he [17] had on, and put on him his own garments. [^n3556]And while they were going with him, they found a man, a Cyrenian, coming from the country, named Simon, the father of Alexander and Rufus: [^n3557]and they compelled this man to bear the cross of Jesus. [18] [^n3558]And they took the cross and laid it upon him, that he might bear it, and come after Jesus; and Jesus went, and his cross behind him.

[19] [^n3559]And there followed him much people, and women which were lamenting and [20] raving.[^n3560] [^n3561]But Jesus turned unto them and said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not [21] for me: weep for yourselves, and for your children. [^n3562]Days are coming, when they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that bare not, and the breasts [22] that gave not suck. [^n3563]Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and [23] to the hills, Cover us. [^n3564]For if they do so in the green tree,[^n3565] what shall be in the dry?
[24] [^n3566]And they brought with Jesus two others of the malefactors,[^n3567] to be put to death.

[25] [^n3568]And when they came unto a certain place called The skull, and called in the Hebrew Golgotha, they crucified him there: [^n3569]they crucified with him these two [26] malefactors, one on his right, and the other on his left. [^n3570]And the scripture was [27] [Arabic, p. 194] fulfilled, which saith, He was numbered with the transgressors. [^n3571]And they gave him to drink wine and myrrh, and vinegar which had been mixed with the myrrh; [^n3572]and he tasted, and would not drink; and he received it not.

[28] [^n3573]And the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments, and cast lots for them in four parts, to every party of the soldiers a part; and his tunic was [29] without sewing, from the top woven throughout. [^n3574]And they said one to another, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: and the scripture was fulfilled, which saith,
They divided my garments among them,
And cast the lot for my vesture.

[30, 31] [^n3575]This the soldiers did. And they sat and guarded him there. [^n3576]And Pilate wrote on a tablet the cause of his death, and put it on the wood of the cross above his head.[^n3577] And there was written upon it thus: This is Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the [32] Jews. [^n3578]And this tablet[^n3579] read many of the Jews: for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city: and it was written in Hebrew and Greek and Latin. [33] [^n3580]And the chief priests said unto Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but, He it is [34] that[^n3581] said, I am the King of the Jews. [^n3582]Pilate said unto them, What hath been [35] written hath been written.[^n3583] [^n3584]And the people were standing beholding; and they [36] that passed by were reviling[^n3585] him, and shaking[^n3586] their heads, and saying, [^n3587]Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, [^n3588]save thyself if thou art the Son [37] of God, and come down from the cross. [^n3589]And in like manner the chief priests and the [Arabic, p. 195] scribes and the elders and the Pharisees derided him, and laughed one with [38, 39] another, and said, [^n3590]The saviour of others cannot save himself. [^n3591]If he is the Messiah, the chosen of God, and the King of Israel,[^n3592] let him come down now from the [40] cross, that we may see, and believe in him. [^n3593]He that relieth on God—let him deliver him [41] now, if he is pleased with him: for he said, I am the Son of God. [^n3594]And the soldiers [42] also scoffed at him in that they came near unto him, [^n3595]and brought him vinegar, and [43] said unto him, If thou art the King of the Jews, save thyself. [^n3596]And likewise the two robbers[^n3597] also that were crucified with him reproached him.

[44] [^n3598]And one of those two malefactors who were crucified with him reviled him, and [45] said, If thou art the Messiah, save thyself, and save us also. [^n3599]But his comrade rebuked him, and said, Dost thou not even fear God, being thyself also in this [46] condemnation? [^n3600]And we with justice, and as we deserved, and according to our deed,[^n3601] have we been rewarded: but this man hath not done anything unlawful. [47] [^n3602]And he said unto Jesus, Remember me, my Lord, when thou comest in thy kingdom. [48] [^n3603]Jesus said unto him, Verily[^n3604] I say unto thee, To-day shalt thou be with me in Paradise.

[49] [^n3605]And there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister,[^n3606] [50] Mary[^n3607] that was related to Clopas, and Mary Magdalene. [^n3608]And Jesus saw his mother, and that disciple whom he loved standing by; and he said to his mother, [51] Woman, behold, thy son! [^n3609]And he said to that disciple, Behold, thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto himself.

[52] [Arabic, p. 196] [^n3610]And from the sixth hour[^n3611] darkness was on all the land unto the ninth [53] hour,[^n3612] and the sun became dark. [^n3613]And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, and said, Yail, Yaili,[^n3614] why hast thou forsaken me? which[^n3615] is, My [54] God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? [^n3616]And some of those that stood there, when they heard, said,[^n3617] This man called Elijah.

n3539.text: cf. Peshitta. Or, Ye know (cf. Sinaitic).

n3545.text: Borg. ms. omits and he went away.

n3560.text: Lit. being burned. The text is probably corrupt.

n3579.text: A different word from that in the preceding verse; in each case, the word used in the Peshitta (Cur. and Sin. lacking).

n3581.text: The Syriac words, retained in Ibn-at-Tayyib’s Commentary (f. 366a), seem to have been transposed. Vat. ms. omits he, probably meaning but that he said.

n3583.text: In a carelessly written Arabic ms. there is almost no difference between hath been written and I have written, as it is in Ibn-at-Tayyib (loc. cit., f. 366a).

n3585.text: cf. § 7, 17, note. Borg. ms. has jesting at.

n3586.text: The Arabic text has deriding (cf. § 51, 37). Either with is accidentally omitted, or, more probably, we should correct the spelling to shaking (cf. Syriac versions).

n3597.text: Borg. ms. has boys (an easy clerical error).

n3601.text: Our deed might be read we have done, and perhaps our translator’s style would justify our writing as for to.

n3611.text: Lit six hours and nine hours respectively.

n3612.text: Lit six hours and nine hours respectively.

n3614.text: In Vat. ms. the second word is like the first. The syllable Ya doubtless is the Arabic interjection O!

n3615.text: The Borg. ms. omits from which to me.

n3617.text: Borg. ms. omits when they, and has and said.
